summary: Overall high quality and appropriately hedged. Every numeric key was recomputed (HbA1c conversion, PDC, units, PPV, LR post-test probability, LAeq, attributable fraction, UPC, pack-years, weight loss, rate ratio, excess admissions, incidence, prevalence, genetic risk) and all are correct with sensible tolerances; every MCQ and true/false key is the single correct option. NICE (NG28, NG136, NG59, NG12, NG5), screening programmes and immunisation are referred to without stating ages, intervals or thresholds as fact, and alcohol (14 units), activity (150 minutes) and hierarchy of controls statements are correct. Only minor consistency and precision points were found; no encoding or LaTeX defects were detected. This is an AI review: the course still needs a subject-matter expert before clinical reliance.

issues.problem: Explanation says 'Personalised care adjustment (exception reporting) exists...'. QOF exception reporting was replaced by personalised care adjustment in 2019/20, so the two terms are not equivalent. Unverified for the current QOF year.
issues.suggestedFix: Refer to 'personalised care adjustment (formerly called exception reporting)' and check against the current QOF guidance.

issues.problem: Back pain age red flag is given three ways: lesson text 'under 20 or over 50 to 55', table 'under 20 or over 55', and q009 marking guide 'age over 55'. NG59 itself does not set a specific age list, so these are teaching conventions presented inconsistently.
issues.suggestedFix: Use one wording across lesson, table and marking guide (for example 'under 20 or over 55, commonly used teaching threshold') and note that thresholds vary by source.

issues.problem: Noise worked example concludes that at about 92 dB(A) 'the employer must control the noise and offer hearing protection and health surveillance (check current HSE levels)'. The lesson never states the HSE action values, and the duties differ by level (lower value 80 dB(A): provide hearing protection on request and information; upper value 85 dB(A): reduce exposure by controls, mandatory hearing protection zones, health surveillance).
issues.suggestedFix: State the lower (80 dB(A)) and upper (85 dB(A)) daily or weekly LEP,d action values and the peak values (135 and 137 dB(C)) from the Control of Noise at Work Regulations 2005, and say 92 dB(A) exceeds the upper action value. Verify against current HSE guidance.

issues.problem: Summary and q010 marking guide use 'rolling with resistance' (older MI terminology), which the lesson text never introduces.
issues.suggestedFix: Either add a sentence on sustaining versus discord/resistance in the lesson or remove the phrase from the summary and marking guide.
